kept.title: Unbounded Buffer Accumulation via Header Folding
kept.description: The HeaderParser in deps/dicer/lib/HeaderParser.js handles folded header content (lines starting with tab/space) by appending them to existing header values without explicit size checks beyond the total header size, potentially allowing for large memory consumption.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a multipart request with a header key.
Send large amounts of folded whitespace or data across multiple lines.
Cause memory exhaustion by exceeding system constraints through repeated header expansion.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) due to excessive memory consumption.

kept.title: Unbounded Memory Allocation in Field Parsing
kept.description: In lib/types/urlencoded.js, the field key and value accumulation uses simple string concatenation that can exceed memory limits before the limit-check logic is fully effective, especially when handling maliciously large streams of encoded characters.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request with an extremely long field name or value string.
Ensure the stream does not immediately hit the byte count check for every character.
Force the accumulation of massive strings in the _key or _val properties.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Use of unsafe Buffer.allocUnsafe
kept.description: The code uses Buffer.allocUnsafe in several benchmark and helper files to create memory buffers without zero-initializing them.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an operation that uses these buffers (e.g., multipart creation).
If the memory space contains sensitive data from previous operations, it may be leaked into the buffer content.
The leaked data could be exposed in subsequent operations if this buffer is used.
kept.impact: Information disclosure; potential leakage of process memory contents.

kept.title: Path Traversal via Unsafe Filename Handling
kept.description: The basename utility does not sufficiently protect against various character encodings or bypass techniques that could lead to filename manipulation in environments where output paths are user-controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a filename that includes encoded path characters.
The utility logic for slicing paths might be bypassed in specific platform implementations.
Attempt to escape intended directories if the result is used to save files on disk.
kept.impact: Arbitrary file path modification or traversal.

kept.title: Potential Prototype Pollution via Object.create(null)
kept.description: While Object.create(null) is used to avoid prototype pollution, the manual construction and population of these objects from user-provided content in HeaderParser can still lead to property collisions if logic errors occur.
steps_to_exploit: Submit headers that mimic internal property names.
Observe if the object population logic allows property overriding that affects downstream processing.
kept.impact: Logic bypass or unexpected behavior within the parser state.

kept.title: Insecure Temporary Directory Usage
kept.description: The parted-multipart benchmark implementation uses /tmp or C:/Temp as a hardcoded default for file streams, which is prone to race conditions or symlink attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Predict a temporary file name if the generation logic is weak.
Pre-create a symlink in the temporary directory to point to a sensitive system file.
Wait for the process to write into the symlinked file.
kept.impact: Arbitrary file overwrite or unauthorized access to system files.

kept.title: Lack of Validation in Benchmark Utilities
kept.description: The contestantResolver.js uses user-supplied command-line arguments to access object properties via index or key without strict validation.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a malicious contestant index.
If accessible via web wrappers, this could lead to property access errors or information exposure of the contestant object structure.
kept.impact: Denial of Service or internal object structure disclosure.

kept.title: Denial of Service via Unbounded Recursion/Loop
kept.description: The getDecoder logic uses a `while(true)` loop that only exits upon specific matches or a flag flip, creating a potential risk for infinite loops if `charset` processing logic fails or is malformed.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a request with an obscure character set string that triggers the `default` switch case repeatedly.
Verify the state transition logic.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via CPU exhaustion.

kept.title: Potential Integer Overflow in Limit Checks
kept.description: The byte counters like `this.nread` or `this.npairs` are not explicitly protected against integer overflow, which could lead to logic bypasses in limit enforcement.
steps_to_exploit: Send a stream large enough to overflow the numeric representation.
Observe if the limit-check condition becomes negative or behaves unexpectedly.
kept.impact: Bypass of security limits (e.g., header size, file size).

kept.title: Unbounded Field Count Logic
kept.description: The multipart parser allows an unlimited number of parts if the configuration is missing or malformed, potentially leading to memory exhaustion.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request with thousands of tiny fields.
Exhaust system memory by having the parser track all these as distinct parts.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Incomplete Validation of Content-Transfer-Encoding
kept.description: The multipart parser accepts various encodings without verifying their safety or potential for memory-intensive transformations.
steps_to_exploit: Use unusual or heavy encoding strings in headers.
Examine how the parser attempts to decode these streams.

kept.title: Use of unsafe String encoding in Decoder
kept.description: The Decoder uses `String.fromCharCode(parseInt(this.buffer, 16))` which can fail or produce unexpected results for non-UTF8 input character sets.
steps_to_exploit: Provide malformed percent-encoded characters in a stream.
Observe if the parser handles the resulting character correctly or throws an error.
kept.impact: Parser crashes or misinterpretation of input data.

kept.title: Weak Randomness for Temporary Files
kept.description: The temporary file naming logic uses `Math.random()` which is not cryptographically secure, making temporary files predictable.
steps_to_exploit: Estimate the sequence of random numbers being generated.
Pre-emptively create files that the system might attempt to create.
kept.impact: Predictable file name generation, facilitating DoS or data exposure.

kept.title: Potential Data Truncation Misreporting
kept.description: The logic for emitting 'limit' events and setting `truncated` flags can be bypassed or result in inconsistent states if multiple stream chunks are handled out of order or concurrently.
steps_to_exploit: Send chunks that intentionally straddle the size limit boundary.
Observe if the `file.truncated` flag is set correctly and if `limit` events fire.
kept.impact: Incorrect API usage, potentially allowing payloads that exceed configured limits.

kept.title: Unsafe Header Value Slicing
kept.description: Header parsing uses `buffer.slice` without considering the character encoding context, which may lead to partial multi-byte character corruption.
steps_to_exploit: Send headers containing UTF-8 characters that are split across buffer chunks.
Check if the resulting strings contain invalid characters or are malformed.
kept.impact: Incorrect parsing of header information, causing logic errors.
